title: Marketing philosophies: production, product and selling concepts
summary: The five marketing concepts on the overview diagram, then the production, product and selling concepts: what each holds, its strategy, pros and cons.

chunks.heading: Marketing philosophies at a glance
chunks.explanation_md:
Under the heading **Marketing Philosophies and Orientation**, the slide puts **Marketing Concepts** at the centre with **five concepts** around it:

1. **The production concept**
2. **The product concept**
3. **The selling concept**
4. **The marketing concept**
5. **The social marketing concept** (its own slide later calls it the **Societal Marketing Concept**)

The deck also covers the **Holistic Marketing Concept**, which is not one of the five circles.

This topic covers the first three. For each one, learn the same things from the slides: **what it holds**, its **marketing strategy**, its **pros** and its **cons**.
chunks.exam_line: The overview diagram shows five marketing concepts: production, product, selling, marketing and social (societal) marketing concept.

chunks.heading: The production concept
chunks.explanation_md:
**What it holds:** this concept **focuses on the internal capabilities of the firm** rather than on the desires and needs of the marketplace. It **works on an assumption that consumers prefer a product which is inexpensive and widely available**.

**Marketing strategy:** **production efficiency**.

**It holds in these situations:**
1. **Demand exceeds supply**
2. **Product cost is too high**

**Pros:**
1. **Economies of scale**
2. **Decreased production cost**

**Cons:**
1. **No focus on product quality**
2. **Does not consider needs of the marketplace**

key_terms.meaning: Focuses on the internal capabilities of the firm rather than the desires and needs of the marketplace; assumes consumers prefer products that are inexpensive and widely available.

chunks.exam_line: Production concept: focus on internal capabilities; assumes consumers prefer inexpensive, widely available products; strategy is production efficiency; holds when demand exceeds supply or product cost is too high; pros economies of scale and decreased production cost; cons no focus on quality and ignores marketplace needs.

chunks.heading: The product concept
chunks.explanation_md:
**What it holds:** consumers will **favour products that offer the most in quality, performance and features**.

**Marketing strategy:** **continuous product improvements**.

**Pros:**
1. **Improved product quality**

**Cons:**
1. It can **fail to appeal to customers whose demands are driven by other factors** like **price, availability, usability**, etc.
2. It **leads to marketing myopia**, focusing on fulfilment of the **immediate needs of the company**.

Recall the definition of **marketing myopia** from earlier in the deck: focusing only on existing wants and losing sight of underlying consumer needs.

key_terms.meaning: Holds that consumers will favour products that offer the most in quality, performance and features.

chunks.exam_line: Product concept: consumers favour products with the most quality, performance and features; strategy is continuous product improvements; pro improved quality; cons it misses customers driven by price, availability or usability, and it leads to marketing myopia.

chunks.heading: The selling concept
chunks.explanation_md:
**What it holds:** **people will buy more goods and services if aggressive sales techniques are used**. Its **main focus is to make money**.

**Marketing strategy:** **aggressive selling of products that firms make**.

**Pros:**
1. **High sales of products, especially unsought products**

**Cons:**
1. **Lack of understanding of marketplace needs and wants**
2. It **doesn't include building relations with customers**, hence **repeated sales are very less**

Note the wording of the strategy: it sells the products **that firms make**. The comparison arrow later in the deck shows the same thing: the selling concept starts at the **factory** and focuses on **existing products**.

key_terms.meaning: Based on the idea that people will buy more goods and services if aggressive sales techniques are used; main focus is to make money.

chunks.exam_line: Selling concept: people buy more if aggressive sales techniques are used; main focus is to make money; strategy is aggressive selling of products that firms make; pro high sales, especially of unsought products; cons no understanding of needs and wants, and no relationship building, so repeated sales are very less.

clarification.text: These are products that buyers do not normally think of buying or do not actively look for.
